modules.name: videos

testMatrix.notes: Key retrieval authentication and session validation
Playback token generation and entitlement verification
Heartbeat watch duration accumulation and limit enforcement
HLS master manifest delivery and rewriting
Media segment streaming and watch limit gating

findings.title: Unauthenticated / Unchecked AES-128 Key Delivery Endpoint Lacks Playback Token Validation
findings.evidence: router.get('/:videoId/key', requireVideoEntitlement, asyncHandler(c.getVideoKey)) calls VideoService.getVideoKey({ video, userId, req }), which verifies User.playbackLocked and WatchLog watch limit, but completely ignores req.query.token and does not verify the existence of an active, valid PlaybackSession.
findings.impact: Any entitled user possessing a standard Bearer JWT can retrieve the raw 16-byte AES-128 DRM key directly without starting a playback session, allowing offline caching and decryption.
findings.reproduction: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <STUDENT_JWT>' http://localhost:5000/api/videos/<VIDEO_ID>/key -> Returns 200 OK with raw 16-byte binary decryption key without initiating PlaybackSession.
findings.remediation: Validate req.query.token against PlaybackSession in VideoService.getVideoKey, verify session.expiresAt > new Date(), session.video == videoId, and session.user == userId before returning key buffer.
findings.regressionTest: Call GET /api/videos/:videoId/key without a valid, unexpired playback session token and assert response is 401/403.

findings.title: Automatic Reactivation of Deactivated Videos in requireVideoEntitlement Middleware
findings.evidence: let video = await Video.findOne({ _id: req.params.videoId, active: true }); if (!video) { video = await Video.findOneAndUpdate({ _id: req.params.videoId, status: 'READY' }, { $set: { active: true } }, { new: true }); }
findings.impact: When an administrator deliberately sets video.active = false, any incoming user request touching requireVideoEntitlement automatically updates the database to active: true, overriding administrative intent.
findings.reproduction: Set video.active = false via admin CMS. Perform GET /api/videos/:videoId/hls/manifest.m3u8 as an entitled user. Database record for video is silently flipped back to active = true.
findings.remediation: Remove the auto-heal write mutation from authorization middleware; return AppError('Video not found', 404, 'NOT_FOUND') if video is inactive.
findings.regressionTest: Query an inactive video with status 'READY' through requireVideoEntitlement and verify that it returns 404 and does not modify active: false in DB.

findings.title: HLS Segment Streaming Endpoint Omits Watch Limit and Quota Verification
findings.evidence: router.get('/:videoId/hls/:segment', requireVideoEntitlement, asyncHandler(c.getHlsSegment)) only executes requireVideoEntitlement, which checks plan ownership. Neither getHlsSegment nor requireVideoEntitlement checks WatchLog.totalWatchedSeconds >= maxAllowedSeconds.
findings.impact: Users whose watch limit has expired can continue streaming all video chunks (.ts) directly from MinIO as long as they retain the encryption key, bypassing all plan watch caps.
findings.reproduction: Consume full watch quota for a video. Issue GET /api/videos/:videoId/hls/res_1080p_seg_000.ts. Server returns 200 OK with video/MP2T content.
findings.remediation: Add watch quota verification middleware to getHlsSegment or validate active non-expired PlaybackSession on segment streaming requests.
findings.regressionTest: Request HLS segment after WatchLog.totalWatchedSeconds exceeds maxAllowedSeconds and verify 403 WATCH_LIMIT_REACHED is returned.

findings.title: HLS Variant Sub-Playlists and Multi-Bitrate ABR Segments Omit Playback Session Token
findings.evidence: getHlsManifest replaces /(segment_\d+\.ts)/g with token query parameter, but TranscodeService outputs ABR segments named res_%v_seg_%03d.ts and sub-playlists res_%v.m3u8. Sub-playlists are piped raw from MinIO without token rewriting in getHlsSegment.
findings.impact: Mobile players (Android/iOS) fail with 401 Unauthorized when requesting variant playlists or segments because token query parameters are omitted and players do not transmit custom Bearer headers.
findings.reproduction: Request GET /api/videos/:videoId/hls/manifest.m3u8?token=<UUID>. Sub-playlist links inside master.m3u8 lack token parameters.
findings.remediation: Update regex to match res_\w+\.m3u8 and res_\w+_seg_\d+\.ts, and perform token injection in getHlsSegment when serving variant .m3u8 playlists.
findings.regressionTest: Request master playlist with token and verify that all sub-playlist URLs and subsequent segment URLs carry the token query parameter.

findings.title: Trivial Bypass and Insecure Substring Matching in Key Delivery Hotlinking Protection
findings.evidence: const origin = req.headers.origin || req.headers.referer || ''; const isAllowed = origin.startsWith(env.clientUrl) || origin.includes('localhost') || origin.includes('pinggy') || origin.includes('trycloudflare'); if (origin && !isAllowed) ...
findings.impact: Requests omitting Origin/Referer (e.g. curl, scrapers, mobile clients) evaluate origin to empty string and bypass checks. Furthermore, origin.includes('localhost') allows domains like attacker-localhost.com.
findings.reproduction: Send GET /api/videos/:videoId/key with Header 'Origin: http://evil-localhost.com' or without Origin/Referer headers; request passes hotlink guard.
findings.remediation: Parse origin with URL parser, remove localhost/tunnel substrings from production logic, and enforce strict origin matching against env.clientUrl.
findings.regressionTest: Send key requests with spoofed origins (e.g. http://localhost.attacker.com) and verify rejection with 403 UNAUTHORIZED_DOMAIN.

findings.title: Unvalidated watch-event Route Allows Arbitrary Watch Seconds and Quota Corruption
findings.evidence: router.post('/:videoId/watch-event', asyncHandler(c.reportWatchEvent)) does not attach validate(watchEventSchema). In VideoService.reportWatchEvent, watchedSeconds = Math.max(0, Math.floor(Number(seconds) || 0)) has no upper bound constraint for type === 'started'.
findings.impact: Clients can submit seconds: 1e9 to exhaust user watch quota in one request, or seconds: Infinity to inject NaN into MongoDB $inc, permanently disabling watch limit enforcement.
findings.reproduction: POST /api/videos/:videoId/watch-event with body { token, type: 'started', seconds: 100000000 }. WatchLog.totalWatchedSeconds increases by 100,000,000.
findings.remediation: Attach validate(watchEventSchema) to watch-event route, and clamp seconds to 0 in type === 'started'.
findings.regressionTest: Submit watch-event with seconds: 99999 and assert validation rejects request with 400 Bad Request.

findings.title: Concurrency Race Condition in reportWatchEvent Allows Double-Counting of Watch History
findings.evidence: if (!session.consumed) { session.consumed = true; await session.save(); ... WatchLog.findOneAndUpdate(...) } uses in-memory check without atomic database CAS.
findings.impact: Concurrent requests with the same session token both observe consumed === false and execute WatchLog increment and history push multiple times.
findings.reproduction: Send 5 concurrent POST requests with type: 'started' using the same token. Multiple requests pass the condition and push duplicate history records.
findings.remediation: Execute atomic update: PlaybackSession.findOneAndUpdate({ _id: session._id, consumed: false }, { $set: { consumed: true } }) and proceed only if a document was modified.
findings.regressionTest: Dispatch 5 parallel 'started' watch-events with the same token and assert only 1 succeeds in recording history.

findings.title: Missing Magic Byte Verification on Raw Video Uploads
findings.evidence: uploadRawVideo only checks path.extname(filename) and mimeType string from client headers. Unlike uploadBookFiles, it does not inspect file magic bytes.
findings.impact: Arbitrary non-video payloads with spoofed MIME types and .mp4 extensions are written to NVMe storage and submitted to ffprobe/ffmpeg child processes.
findings.reproduction: Upload text file renamed to sample.mp4 with Content-Type: video/mp4. File is accepted, stored in /tmp/uploads/, and queued to BullMQ.
findings.remediation: Inspect stream chunk prefix for ISO BMFF / Matroska signatures (ftyp for MP4/MOV, 0x1A45DFA3 for WebM/MKV) before streaming to disk.
findings.regressionTest: Upload an executable renamed to .mp4 and verify middleware rejects it with 415 Unsupported Media Type.

findings.title: Unhandled WriteStream Error in Busboy Video Upload Causes Server Process Crash
findings.evidence: writeStream = fs.createWriteStream(rawFilePath); fileStream.pipe(writeStream); does not attach writeStream.on('error', ...). On disk full (ENOSPC), Node.js crashes with an unhandled stream error.
findings.impact: Uploading files when disk is near full crashes the Node.js API process, causing total service denial.
findings.reproduction: Simulate write error / full filesystem during uploadRawVideo. Unhandled error event on writeStream terminates Node process.
findings.remediation: Attach writeStream.on('error', (err) => { cleanup(err.message); next(new AppError('File write error', 500, 'IO_ERROR')); }).
findings.regressionTest: Emit error on writeStream and verify API responds with 500 without process termination.

findings.title: Premature Temporary Directory Deletion Prevents BullMQ Transcoding Retries
findings.evidence: processTranscodeJob has a finally block executing fs.rmSync(uploadDir, { recursive: true, force: true }). If step 5 (upload to MinIO) fails on attempt 1, uploadDir is deleted, causing BullMQ attempts 2 and 3 to immediately fail with file not found.
findings.impact: Transient worker failures (MinIO timeout, Redis hiccup) cannot be recovered by BullMQ retry mechanisms.
findings.reproduction: Simulate network error during MinIO upload. Attempt 1 deletes uploadDir in finally. BullMQ retries and fails with 'Raw video file not found'.
findings.remediation: Only delete uploadDir in finally if job succeeded or if job.attemptsMade >= job.opts.attempts.
findings.regressionTest: Fail attempt 1 of transcode job and verify rawFilePath remains intact for attempt 2.

findings.title: FFmpeg ABR Pipeline Fails on Videos Without Audio Tracks or Non-H.264 Codecs
findings.evidence: Stream copy (-c:v:0 copy) breaks on VP9/ProRes because MPEG-TS container does not support VP9. Furthermore, -var_stream_map explicitly maps a:0, a:1, a:2, which crashes FFmpeg on silent videos without audio.
findings.impact: Silent screen captures and WebM/MKV uploads fail transcoding completely.
findings.reproduction: Upload silent MP4 with no audio stream. FFmpeg exits with code 1: 'Stream map a:0 matches no streams'.
findings.remediation: Inspect probeMetadata output; if no audio stream exists, omit audio maps from -var_stream_map. Re-encode stream 0 if codec is not h264.
findings.regressionTest: Transcode a silent video and verify TranscodeService completes successfully.

findings.title: Encryption Key and Storage Path Discrepancy Between HlsService and TranscodeService
findings.evidence: TranscodeService saves a random 16-byte key to video.encryptionKeyHex in MongoDB, while HlsService uses deterministic HMAC and does not set encryptionKeyHex. Re-transcoding with HlsService leaves the old encryptionKeyHex in DB while files are encrypted with the HMAC key.
findings.impact: Calling POST /:videoId/transcode-hls on an existing video breaks client playback permanently due to key mismatch.
findings.reproduction: Upload video via TranscodeService (writes encryptionKeyHex). Call POST /api/videos/:id/transcode-hls. Key returned by getVideoKey no longer decrypts stream.
findings.remediation: Align HlsService to use TranscodeService's key generation and storage logic, or retire HlsService in favor of TranscodeService.
findings.regressionTest: Re-transcode video via HlsService and assert served decryption key matches media segments.

findings.title: HTTP Headers Already Sent Exception in Realtime SSE Connection Limiter
findings.evidence: publicController.events flushes SSE headers and writes ': connected\n\n' before calling addRealtimeClient(res). Inside addRealtimeClient, if clients.size >= MAX_SSE_CLIENTS, it attempts res.status(429).json(...), triggering ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT.
findings.impact: Server throws unhandled ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT exceptions when SSE capacity is reached.
findings.reproduction: Open 100 SSE connections, then open connection 101. Express crashes with ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT.
findings.remediation: Check clients.size before setting headers and writing data in publicController.events.
findings.regressionTest: Exceed MAX_SSE_CLIENTS and assert client 101 receives 429 without header errors.

findings.title: Missing ObjectId Validation on Video Route Parameters Leads to Unhandled Cast Errors
findings.evidence: Routes in videos.js do not validate req.params.videoId against objectIdParamSchema. Malformed parameter values trigger Mongoose CastError resulting in 500 Internal Server Error.
findings.impact: Triggers unhandled 500 errors and reveals database stack traces on malformed requests.
findings.remediation: Add validate(objectIdParamSchema, 'params') to all parameterized routes in routes/videos.js.
findings.regressionTest: Send GET /api/videos/123/key and verify response is 400 Bad Request.

verdictNotes: At least one verified open Critical/High finding exists.
